subject: Regional presence dependencies & fallback strategies for data residency
messages:
From: Emily Rossi <emily.rossi@medicloudhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Medicloud Security Team <security@medicloudhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: clarifications on regional data residency and acceptable fallback behaviors

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the RFP packet you sent yesterday. Our procurement team reviewed the product capability questionnaire and flagged a few clarifications we need before advancing to legal. High level: Medicloud requires customer data for EU residents to remain in EU jurisdictions unless an explicit, auditable fallback is invoked. We want to understand:

- Which Redwood deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private) can guarantee EU-only storage and processing?
- If hosted, do you provide regional tenancy segmentation or a geo-routing guarantee?
- In scenarios where EU capacity is unavailable, what fallback strategies do you support and how are they logged/audited?
- For APAC, we have both Singapore and Japan preferences — can you map which regions you operate in and whether data can be pinned to a region?

Could you provide a concise matrix and any supporting artifacts (SOC 2 evidence, network diagrams) that we can attach to our security assessment? We're on a tight timeline for our procurement committee (decision window end of month).

Appreciate a short doc and a follow-up call if useful.

Best,
Emily
Director of Cloud Ops, Medicloud Health

Attachment: Medicloud_RFP_Section_B_DataResidency.docx (referenced)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
To: Emily Rossi <emily.rossi@medicloudhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: clarifications on regional data residency and acceptable fallback behaviors

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned on timing and can get you a concise matrix plus artifacts by end of day Wednesday PST. Summary up front:

- Hosted API: regional pinning (EU-only) is supported via our EU-hosted clusters; we provide a data residency guarantee when a customer elects the EU tenancy during onboarding.
- Dedicated: full guarantee (customer-dedicated GPU pools and persistent storage in your chosen region).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full control — can be deployed inside your VPC in SG/JP/EU as required.

Fallbacks: hosted offers automated routed fallbacks (same-region preferred, then dedicated or private if configured). We log each fallback with a traceable event id and record in audit logs. I'll attach our residency matrix and SOC 2 stub; Lauren will add the network topology.

Propose a 30-min call Wed 10:00 AM CET or 2:00 PM CET — what works?

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_data_residency_matrix_v1.xlsx (matrix), SOC2-Type2-Redwood-2025.pdf (cert stub)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>, Emily Rossi <emily.rossi@medicloudhealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: network topology and region mapping + notes on regional tenancy

Forwarding the topology and some implementation notes. Key points to call out in the RFP response:

- EU tenancy: when a customer selects EU tenancy, throughput endpoints and storage are provisioned on EU regions only (currently FR, IE). We offer a contract clause to restrict cross-border replication.
- APAC: we have SG (Singapore) and JP (Tokyo) regional nodes available as private deployments; hosted EU tenancy does not automatically replicate to APAC without explicit policy.
- Fallback logging: when any automated routing sends traffic outside the pinned region (rare, e.g., region outage), the event is written to audit logs and a field-level flag (region_override=true) is emitted in request traces; those trace ids are retained for 13 months by default and can be extended.

See attached network diagram for how public-hosted control plane interacts with customer tenancy.

--Lauren
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_vpc_network_topology.svg (network diagram)

From: Emily Rossi <emily.rossi@medicloudhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Medicloud Security Team <security@medicloudhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 13:14:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Fwd: network topology and region mapping + notes on regional tenancy

Thanks Jordan and Lauren — the matrix is helpful. A few follow-ups from security:

1) Can you confirm the SLA / contractual language for "data residency guarantee"? Our legal will want explicit wording that data at rest and processing for EU residents will not leave EU without written authorization.
2) In the fallback scenario, we need the exact audit event format and where those logs reside (Redwood console vs. a customer-pushed S3/GCS bucket). Is the event ID sufficient for us to tie an incident to on-prem logs?
3) For APAC, we need options: (a) hosted EU tenancy + edge inference in APAC with only ephemeral KV cache (no persistent data); (b) dedicated APAC pods; (c) private deployment in our GCP SG region. Which of these are currently supported and which incur additional engineering time?

Also, can you attach your SOC 2 report and a sample contract clause? That will speed legal review.

--Emily

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 07:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: network topology and region mapping + notes on regional tenancy

Hi Emily — quick technical clarifications to help legal and security:

1) Contract wording we propose (high level): "Redwood will store and process Personal Data originating from EU residents solely within EU regions selected by the Customer. Redwood will not transfer such Personal Data outside the European Economic Area (EEA) except where (a) Customer has provided prior written authorization, or (b) automatic fallback is invoked due to a verified regional outage; any such fallback events will be logged and notified to the Customer within 24 hours." We can provide a full draft clause for legal redlines.

2) Audit event format and delivery: fallback events are emitted with a structured JSON record: {event_id, timestamp, affected_tenants, original_region, executed_region, reason_code, trace_id}. We can push logs to a customer-managed S3/GCS bucket (recommended) or make them visible in the Redwood Console. Trace ids are correlated with the request traces. Retention: default 13 months; custom retention and export available via Dedicated/Private offerings.

3) APAC options: (a) hosted EU tenancy + APAC edge for ephemeral KV cache — supported today as a beta; ephemeral caches never persist to durable storage, but we treat edge logs as a separate telemetry stream that can be disabled. (b) Dedicated APAC pods — available, requires capacity reservation lead time (typically 4-8 weeks). (c) Private deployment in customer GCP SG — supported and generally the fastest to satisfy strict data residency; professional services assist onboarding (2-4 weeks).

Engineering impact: (a) minor config + opt-in; (b) moderate provisioning + capacity booking; (c) standard private deployment engagement with security handshake (NDA, network whitelisting, KMS integration).

I've attached a SOC2 stub and the residency matrix in single package for legal. Happy to join a call to walk legal through the clause.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOC2-Type2-Redwood-2025.pdf (cert stub); redwood_data_residency_matrix_v1.xlsx (matrix)
